neighbours.label: the modifier just before an expected 'allowance' / 'stipend' / 'pension' when someone is given a small regular payment (a small weekly ..., a monthly ..., a modest living ...); the pole's output promotes ' allowance', ' stip', ' pocket'
fire: When I turned ten, my father started paying me a small weekly allowance.
The fellowship comes with a monthly stipend for housing and food.
Volunteers in the program are given a modest living allowance.
His grandmother sent him a little monthly allowance while he was at college.
Each child in the family earned a weekly allowance for doing chores.
Interns at the firm are paid a small monthly stipend instead of a salary.
The widow was left to survive on a tiny weekly pension.
Exchange students get a daily allowance to cover meals and bus fares.
quiet: When I turned ten, my father started taking me to the weekly market.
The fellowship holds a monthly seminar on housing and food policy.
Volunteers in the program are given a clean uniform and a badge.
His grandmother wrote him a long letter every month while he was at college.
Each child in the family did chores on Saturday mornings.
Interns at the firm attend a weekly meeting with the partners.
The widow was left to look after a tiny farm by herself.
Exchange students take a daily bus to the campus across town.

notes: Card: peaks ' monthly', ' stip', ' weekly', ' small' before allowance. Probe: 'small weekly allowance' 1.26, 'modest living allowance' 0.99, 'monthly stipend' 0.72; 'monthly newsletter' 0.01, 'weekly paper' 0.02. The + pole is ' $' before an income figure.
